judge-s-bench.definition: The raised desk or platform where the judge sits in a courtroom.
judge-s-bench.exampleUsage: The judge entered and took a seat at the judge's bench.

witness-stand.definition: An enclosed area in a courtroom where a witness gives evidence while answering questions.

jury-box.definition: A separate area in a courtroom where the members of a jury sit during a trial.

defense-table.definition: The courtroom table where the defendant and defense legal team sit during a trial.
defense-table.exampleUsage: The defense lawyers organized their documents at the defense table.

prosecution-table.definition: The courtroom table where the prosecution legal team sits during a trial.
prosecution-table.exampleUsage: The prosecutor placed case files on the prosecution table.

gallery.definition: The area of a courtroom where members of the public sit.

bar.definition: A barrier separating the public area from the working area of a courtroom.

clerk-s-desk.definition: The courtroom desk used by the court clerk, who manages records and procedural documents.
clerk-s-desk.exampleUsage: The court clerk sat at the clerk's desk.

bailiff-s-post.definition: The position or area in a courtroom assigned to the bailiff responsible for order and security.
bailiff-s-post.exampleUsage: The bailiff remained at the assigned post during the hearing.

podium.definition: A platform raised above the surrounding level to give prominence to the person on it.

judge.definition: A public official authorized to decide questions brought before a court of justice.

jury.definition: A body of citizens sworn to give a true verdict according to the evidence presented in a court of law.

plaintiff.definition: A person who brings an action in a court of law.

defendant.definition: A person or institution against whom an action is brought in a court of law.

witness.definition: A person who sees an event or gives evidence in court.

bailiff.definition: A court officer who helps maintain courtroom order and security; duties vary by jurisdiction.

court-reporter.definition: A professional who creates an official word-for-word record of court proceedings.
court-reporter.exampleUsage: The court reporter recorded the testimony.

clerk.definition: A court employee who maintains records and assists with court administration.

foreman.definition: The member who leads a jury and speaks for it in court; also called the jury foreperson.

expert-witness.definition: A witness allowed to give specialized opinion evidence because of relevant knowledge, training, or experience.
expert-witness.exampleUsage: The expert witness explained the technical evidence.

opening-statement.definition: An introductory explanation of what a side expects to show in a trial.

testimony.definition: Evidence given by a witness, usually under oath.

cross-examination.definition: Questioning of a witness by the opposing side after that witness has given direct testimony.
cross-examination.exampleUsage: The attorney began cross-examination after direct testimony ended.

objection.definition: (law) a procedure whereby a party to a suit says that a particular line of questioning or a particular witness or a piece of evidence or other matter is improper and should not be continued and asks the court to rule on its impropriety or illegality.

sustained.definition: Used when a judge accepts an objection.

overruled.definition: Used when a judge rejects an objection.

closing-argument.definition: A final statement in which each side summarizes its case and interpretation of the evidence for the judge or jury.
closing-argument.exampleUsage: The lawyers presented closing arguments at the end of the trial.

deliberation.definition: Careful discussion by a jury before it reaches a decision.

verdict.definition: (law) the findings of a jury on issues of fact submitted to it for decision.

sentencing.definition: The stage of a criminal case in which a court formally decides and imposes a lawful sentence after conviction.
sentencing.exampleUsage: The judge scheduled sentencing for a later date.

exhibit.definition: An object or statement produced before a court of law and referred to while giving evidence.

document.definition: A written or printed record, including one stored electronically.

photograph.definition: A picture made with a camera to record a person, place, or event.

video.definition: A recording of moving images that may be presented as evidence.

dna-evidence.definition: Information obtained by examining genetic material and used as evidence.

fingerprint.definition: A print made by an impression of the ridges in the skin of a finger.

deposition.definition: Recorded testimony usually taken under oath before a trial.
deposition.arabicTranslation: شهادة مسجلة تحت القسم قبل المحاكمة

forensic-evidence.definition: Information obtained through scientific examination for an investigation or legal case.
